- Over-forecasting tends to occur when sentiment is negative or volatile in the recent 18-day window, especially if sentiment dips below -0.30; model should reduce early peaks.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in the last 3–5 days, model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment is bullish.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast spike, model likely missed mean reversion; apply downward bias correction if sentiment turns negative within 5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates short-term volatility; if sentiment is erratic or negative, reduce forecast slope or add smoothing to avoid overfitting to recent highs.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to overcorrect upward; apply downward bias adjustment of 0.5–1.0 units to forecast if sentiment < -0.30 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If forecast is >1.5 standard deviation above recent 18-day mean, and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7 units to avoid overconfidence bias.
